findings.issue: The test hard-codes a 3000-level well-formed document and asserts `strict_json(data) is not None`. That only works where CPython's C recursion limit is above 3000. CPython 3.12 sets C_RECURSION_LIMIT to 3000 on _WIN32 (10000 on Linux), and 3.13 also uses 3000 on Windows and 1000 on Windows ARM64. Each nesting level costs one Py_EnterRecursiveCall, plus a few levels of caller overhead. So on Windows, json.loads of 3000 levels raises RecursionError, the new strict_json turns it into ValueError, and the test's precondition assert raises. Both the [array] and [object] cases then fail in the gating `QA and Windows standalone` job (.github/workflows/qa-windows.yml runs `python -m pytest -q` on windows-latest with Python 3.12). The report's open-risks line says 'The tests do not depend on that number'. That is wrong for this test.
findings.reproduction: Linux probe with the worktree sources: strict_json(closed(d)) parses at d=9990 and raises 'ValueError: JSON nesting limit exceeded' at d=9998, which is C limit 10000 minus a few levels of overhead. /usr/include/python3.12/cpython/pystate.h:265-266 has `#  elif defined(_WIN32)` / `#    define C_RECURSION_LIMIT 3000`, and /usr/include/python3.13/cpython/pystate.h:215-216 has the same 3000. On Windows 3.12, d=3000 is past the limit, so `assert strict_json(data) is not None` raises ValueError before the code under test runs.
findings.fix: Choose a depth that is above the Python frame limit but well below the smallest C limit, for example `depth = sys.getrecursionlimit() + 500` (1500 at the default). Checked: closed(1500, 'object') raises RecursionError from _finite on base 882d1ca0 and ArtifactError on the branch, so the test stays red-then-green. Also fix the closed() docstring so it does not claim a platform-independent property.

findings.issue: The comment says 13,000 levels is 'the deepest object document that still passes the 64 KiB size check'. 13,000 * 5 = 65,000 bytes, but the limit is 65,536 bytes, so 13,107 levels would be the deepest. The test itself is fine.
findings.fix: Change the wording to 'a deep object document that still passes the 64 KiB size check'.

findings.issue: When a well-formed artifact parses but is too deep for the recursive _finite walk, the error says 'not strict JSON: maximum recursion depth exceeded', which describes the parser rather than the walk. It is typed as ArtifactError, and load_artifact maps it to 'no model', so this is only about the message. The author already lists it as an open risk.
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from patchtrace.calibration.artifact import parse_artifact; d=1500; parse_artifact(('{\"a\":'*d+'1'+'}'*d).encode())" raises ArtifactError: not strict JSON: maximum recursion depth exceeded
findings.fix: Optional: catch RecursionError around _finite on its own and raise ArtifactError('artifact nesting too deep'), or make _finite iterative.

Result: 14 failed, 6 passed. All 14 failures are RecursionError itself (6 decoding a JSON array, 6 decoding a JSON object, 1 encoder, 1 from the _finite walk), never an assertion mismatch. This matches the author's red evidence. The 6 base-green cases are guards, as the author says. 2) Green on branch: 20 passed. 3) Adversarial probes (scratchpad/reviews/SEC-A/probe.py): parse_artifact/load_artifact over closed array, object, mixed {"a":[...]} and artifact-wrapped documents at 17 depths from 1 to 60000 (boundaries 499/500/501, 9990/9997/9998/10000) gave 68/68 ArtifactError and load_artifact always gave artifact None. diaphora load_manifest with closed array/object/mixed up to 13000 levels, bare and as a deep diaphora_version field, always gave DiaphoraError. raw_cleanup journal lines with a deep extra field always gave 'malformed' ValueError. is_full_verified with a deep 'format' value always returned False. reports._annotation with a deep 'reason' at 900 to 20000 levels gave valid text up to 9990 and '' from 9997 up, no escape. strict_json and parse_artifact in a threading.Thread gave typed errors. Search cursor: bounded at 512 chars by contract, and comparisons and int() on parsed values do not recurse. 4) Checked the post-parse paths for recursion: model_validate_json(ValidationError), the digest/canonical_json that runs only after strict schema validation, and parse_ledger, which already catches RecursionError. 5) Regressions: 30 test files for the touched modules, with -n 4: 787 passed, 1 skipped. 6) `ruff check src tests tools`: all checks passed. 7) Scope: the diff touches only the 6 owned src files plus the new test file, and the worktree is clean. 8) Portability: read the C_RECURSION_LIMIT definitions in the CPython 3.12 and 3.13 headers and confirmed that qa-windows.yml runs the full suite on windows-latest with Python 3.12. summary: The six src fixes are right and minimal. Each one adds RecursionError to the existing handler or maps it into the module's existing typed error or unreadable value. Valid input behaves the same. They close TB-16 at every non-unified site I probed, including well-formed documents near the parser and frame limits and the second defect class the author found (the recursive _finite walk). The red tests really fail on base 882d1ca0 for the stated reason, and the regression suites and ruff are clean. One test is not portable: test_calibration_artifact_parsed_but_deep uses a 3000-level well-formed document and asserts the parser accepts it. CPython 3.12 and 3.13 on Windows cap C recursion at 3000, so that precondition fails in the gating windows-latest QA job. A depth of sys.getrecursionlimit() + 500 fixes it and keeps the test red on base. There are also two wording nits.
